thread:
owen: Quick sync — customer wants an air-gapped POC but has strict Immutable Image rules. Asking whether we can support chunked bundles + signed delta updates within a 90‑day patch cadence.

maya: Short answer: yes, but there are tradeoffs. We can do a chunked image delivery with signed manifests. Need to confirm HSM/KMS signing workflow and whether customer allows a jumpbox for the initial bootstrap.

alex: if they insist on 90-day patch windows we should plan for larger deltas: tiny diffs + patch-on-boot won't work if network is totally closed. We can provide an offline bundle that unpacks on a bastion and writes images to registry.

owen: @maya can you outline what we need from the customer for signing? also pricing — is there an extra engineering fee for building a one-off bundle tool?

maya: From security side we need: (1) public signing key fingerprint, (2) allowlist for any jumpbox IPs (if used), (3) offline acceptance tests they run and pass, and (4) SCC (security questionnaire) answers about K8s runtime. For signing we can either sign artifacts ourselves (requires cust acceptance and escrow/legal) or provide tooling + key spec so customer signs locally.

alex: On pricing — standard on‑prem license covers the image + installer. One-off packaging/engineering: estimate 4–6 days for chunking + delta generator + validation harness. If they want automatic signed deltas every release, that becomes an ongoing engineering/support add‑on.

owen: example of a minimal signed manifest we can ask them to verify on ingest:```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "bundle_id": "redwood-offline-2026-03",
  "chunks": [
    {"name":"runtime.tar.gz","sha256":"<hash>"},
    {"name":"models.q4_2.tar.gz","sha256":"<hash>"}
  ],
  "signature": "<base64-sig>"
}
```

sarah: ops note — our offline installer needs these ports open if they want telemetry tethering later: 443 egress to telemetry.redwood.ai (optional). If fully sealed, we must disable onboarding telemetry and provide an offline license file.

nowen: customer question re: upgrade cadence: "Can we get critical security fixes faster than their 90-day window?" My recommendation: we can produce emergency-only signed hotfix bundles (manual process) but SLA is different — qualifies as professional services and requires fast-commit pricing.

maya: also flag legal: if we sign bundles on their behalf we need an MSA addendum about key custody and indemnities. If they sign themselves, we provide signing spec and test vectors.

alex: engineering ask — do we have a precedent for a fully-sealed bootstrap that writes directly to air-gapped registry? I think 2 customer engagements did this last year (internal notes). Need to surface the runbooks.

owen: Action items: @maya to send signing spec + sample manifest to customer; @alex to draft SOW scoping 4–6 day packaging + optional hotfix support; @sarah to list exact telemetry/license gating steps. I'll loop legal after we have chosen sign-vs-tooling approach.

maya: will send spec and one-pager by EOD. sample ask for customer to provide: public key, allowed jumpbox approach, acceptance test cases (smoke + perf).

eng-oncall-bot: Deploy scheduled: offline-package-build v1 -> staging at 2026-03-17T03:00Z (dry-run) :information_source:

owen: thanks — I'll reply to the customer with the plan and tentative pricing.

alex: +1, also mention that if they want automated signed delta cadence we should discuss a committed monthly support retainer. :thumbsup:

sarah: and copy security for SCC answers — we should offer to fill the questionnaire with them during the POC kickoff to speed approvals.

nowen: perfect. closing thread when spec lands. :white_check_mark:
